question: When next-token predictors learn analytically solvable constrained random walks, do their internal geometries track the full predictive world state or only the next-step distribution, and how do transformer and recurrent architectures factor those quantities across computation?

key_findings.claim: The three grid-walker processes provide exact, separable targets for full-future state and next-step prediction.
key_findings.evidence: For single-endpoint, double-endpoint, and obstacled length-20 walks, dynamic programming gives exact prefix and next-token distributions. The spatiotemporal state is represented by normalized coordinates and time, while a three-component effective field is a linear basis for mean-centered next-token log probabilities; the obstacle variant deliberately contains positions with identical next steps but different futures.

key_findings.claim: All 36 transformer configurations match the exact Bayes-optimal next-token loss on the training distribution to high precision.
key_findings.evidence: One- and two-layer models with one or two heads and head dimensions 32, 64, or 128 obtain normalized cross-entropy ratios between roughly 1.000004 and 1.000138 across the three walkers. Validation is an exact probability-weighted expectation over all relevant prefixes rather than a sampled estimate.

key_findings.claim: Immediately after first-layer attention, normalized position and time are linearly decodable and explain most between-state mean activation variance.
key_findings.evidence: Affine probes decode the three coordinates and reverse affine fits from those coordinates to state-mean activations reach R-squared 0.86–0.99 in selected models. Across all 36 models, held-out state-class fits at post-attention range from about 0.84 to 0.99.

key_findings.claim: The claim that the geometric statistic essentially spans the activation applies to state-mean between-state geometry, not to individual residual-stream activations.
key_findings.evidence: For target-to-activation fits, all paths sharing a position and time are averaged before regression, explicitly removing within-state path-dependent variance that the coordinates cannot explain. The appendix justifies this as a clean geometric analysis, but the main prose's unqualified span language can be read too broadly.

anchors.section: Appendix D.1 / in-sample versus held-out fits

key_findings.claim: A nearly uniform first attention head averages additive move-direction codes and positional codes, yielding normalized displacement and a time-dependent coordinate.
key_findings.evidence: In the illustrated single-layer, single-head Walker L model, attention is approximately uniform over the causal prefix, token value-write vectors form a two-dimensional compass, and token-position interaction accounts for less than 2 times 10 to the minus 5 of centered value-write variance. Averaging the writes gives a linear function of position divided by time plus a path-independent time code.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: the quantitative first-attention circuit evidence is representative-model evidence, not a complete demonstration of the same mechanism across all 36 transformers.
key_findings.evidence: The near-uniform weights, two-dimensional compass, less-than-2e-5 interaction variance, and additive write derivation are worked out for the illustrated one-layer, one-head, dimension-128 Walker L model. The paper states that the same overall mechanism is observed across the full sweep, but the sweep table reports held-out feature fits rather than per-model attention uniformity, compass alignment, token-position interaction, or circuit equivalence. The broad mechanism claim is therefore plausible but less fully quantified than the representation result.

anchors.section: 4.2 / representative first-layer mechanism and sweep assertion
Appendix D.2 / Table 1 reports feature fits, not circuit diagnostics

key_findings.claim: The proposed three-coordinate description is approximate because log time does not fully capture the learned positional code.
key_findings.evidence: The dominant time-code direction is well fit by log t, but a second principal component of the empirical time centroids retains about 6 percent of variance. Thus the reported coordinate vector is a compact proxy for the learned state, not an exact complete parametrization of post-attention activations.

key_findings.claim: Post-attention state-mean geometry is highly similar across constraints, then becomes more variant-specific after the MLP.
key_findings.evidence: On the intersection of position-time states valid across runs, cross-variant linear CKA is 0.95–0.97 for well-trained variants before the MLP and at least 0.72 in the reported comparisons. Walker L versus one-layer Walker O falls from 0.82 before the MLP to 0.43 afterward.

key_findings.claim: The effective field becomes easily readable near the output, but that particular result is algebraically close to tautological.
key_findings.evidence: Mean-centered next-token logits are a fixed linear transform of the effective field, and the final logits are a linear readout of final normalized activations. The authors explicitly acknowledge that an affine probe onto the effective field at the final LayerNorm saturates almost by construction.

key_findings.claim: Recurrent networks achieve essentially the same predictive optimum and retain both target quantities, but do not expose the transformer's clean world-then-task stage separation.
key_findings.evidence: Sixty LSTM and GRU configurations approach normalized loss 1.0, and linear probes recover both geometric coordinates and effective fields. Reverse fits explain only part of recurrent hidden-state variance, especially for the obstacle process, while recurrent representations are mutually more similar and moderately aligned to transformer states.

key_findings.claim: The architecture-specific two-stage mechanism is descriptive rather than causally established.
key_findings.evidence: The paper uses affine probes, CKA, attention patterns, value-write decomposition, and synthetic-grid propagation, but does not ablate the compass code, patch activations between variants, steer coordinates, or test whether removing the proposed axes selectively changes prediction. One trained model exists per architecture configuration, so seed-level circuit reproducibility is also unmeasured.

anchors.section: Appendix E.1 / one model per configuration

key_findings.claim: The study deliberately measures optimization and in-distribution representation, not generalization or world-model competence under changed environments.
key_findings.evidence: Training samples and exact validation expectations come from the same known process and context length eight; the methods state that validation does not measure generalization. The limitations add that no distribution shift is tested and that generation is confounded with prediction by deterministic state transitions given a token.

anchors.section: Appendix E.1 / context and training distribution

method.core_idea: Construct a finite stochastic process whose full predictive state and next-token logit geometry are analytically known, then compare both quantities with activations before and after attention and MLP computation across constraint variants and architectures.
method.mechanism: Exact path-count dynamic programming defines distributions for length-20 single-endpoint, double-endpoint, and obstacled lattice walks. Decoder-only transformers and LSTM/GRU baselines train on sampled prefixes of context length eight while validation exactly averages over the data distribution. Ordinary least-squares probes map activations to normalized position-time coordinates or effective fields and reverse-map those targets into state-mean activations. Linear CKA compares state-mean representations on common supports. Attention patterns and OV value-write vectors are decomposed into token compass codes and positional time codes, and fitted feature grids are propagated through later layers.
assumptions: The normalized coordinates and time proxy are the most meaningful world-state parametrization among equivalent sufficient statistics.
High linear decodability indicates a functionally organized representation rather than an easily reconstructed input statistic.
State-mean activation geometry captures the computation of interest despite removing path-dependent within-state variance.
Random-fold cross-validation over rows adequately tests linear alignment when equivalent or neighboring states recur.
Linear CKA on the intersection of valid state classes is comparable across different widths and constraint-specific data distributions.
High CKA reflects a shared world-state basis rather than common token embeddings, position encodings, averaging, or architecture.
The illustrated attention/value-write mechanism is stable across trained configurations despite one model per configuration and limited quantitative circuit summaries.
Near-Bayes-optimal loss forces retention of the claimed full state rather than another predictive sufficient representation.
The obstacle degeneracy is enough to separate full-future information from immediate next-step logits over the evaluated context.
Findings from one- and two-layer toy models trained in-distribution inform emergent world representations in larger sequence models.

techniques.role: Computes every prefix probability and conditional next-step distribution without Monte Carlo error.
Defines finite-horizon paths constrained to endpoints and obstacles while preserving analytic predictive structure.
Represents any four-move next-token distribution with three mean-centered log-probability coefficients.
Creates obstacle positions with identical next-step laws but different longer-horizon futures.
Separates target decodability from the stronger claim that a target spans activation variance.
Removes within-state path variation before target-to-activation geometry fits and CKA.
Evaluates selected reverse fits on unseen position-time state rows.
Compares cross-variant state-mean geometries on an ordered intersection of valid states.
Factors value-write vectors into move-specific compass codes and position-specific time codes.
Visualizes how later normalization and MLP stages bend the fitted coordinate manifold toward logits.
Contrasts equally predictive transformer, LSTM, and GRU internal geometries.

evaluations.setting: Thirty-six decoder-only transformers over three length-20 grid-walker variants with context length eight
evaluations.metric: Exact expected next-token cross-entropy divided by ground-truth conditional entropy
evaluations.result: All ratios lie approximately between 1.000004 and 1.000138
evaluations.baseline: Bayes-optimal ratio 1.0 computed from the exact process

evaluations.setting: Post-attention and post-MLP state representations across the full transformer architecture sweep
evaluations.metric: Held-out state-class R-squared for affine mapping from three geometric coordinates to state-mean activations
evaluations.result: Post-attention values are roughly 0.84–0.99 across all 36 models, while post-MLP values are lower and reach 0.078 in one obstacle configuration
evaluations.baseline: Post-MLP residuals and alternative effective-field targets

evaluations.setting: Cross-variant transformer state means on common valid position-time support
evaluations.metric: Pairwise linear CKA before and after the MLP
evaluations.result: Well-trained variants reach 0.95–0.97 before the MLP; Walker L versus one-layer Walker O drops from 0.82 before to 0.43 after
evaluations.baseline: Within-variant pairs and post-MLP cross-variant geometry

evaluations.setting: Representative one-layer, one-head Walker L transformer
evaluations.metric: Attention uniformity, value-write geometry, and variance of token-position interaction
evaluations.result: The head approximately averages the prefix, move codes form a two-dimensional compass, and token-position interaction contributes less than 2e-5 of centered value-write variance

evaluations.setting: Sixty LSTM and GRU models across cell type, depth, hidden width, and walker variant
evaluations.metric: Normalized predictive loss, bidirectional probe R-squared, and CKA
evaluations.result: Moderate and wide recurrent models approach Bayes-optimal loss and decode both targets, but target-to-activation fits explain less hidden-state variance and recurrent geometries cluster separately from transformer stages
evaluations.baseline: Transformer sweep and exact optimal loss

limitations: Author-stated: the analytical result is obtained in an intentionally simple toy system and requires new decompositions when predictive structure lacks a closed form.
Author-stated: deterministic transitions given a step confound prediction and generation; hidden-state or formal-language processes are needed to separate them.
Author-stated: no distribution shift or length generalization is tested.
Reviewer-identified: the strongest activation-span result uses state means, removing precisely the within-state variance that a complete statement about activations must explain.
Reviewer-identified: log time leaves about 6 percent of time-code variance in a second component, so the chosen three-coordinate proxy is not exact.
Reviewer-identified: final effective-field decodability is nearly guaranteed by the linear unembedding and fixed logit transform.
Reviewer-identified: common-support restriction and state averaging can raise cross-variant CKA by discarding constraint-specific and path-specific variation.
Reviewer-identified: one trained model per architecture configuration gives no same-configuration seed replication or circuit stability estimate.

Reviewer-identified: the detailed uniform-attention, compass-code, and additive-write measurements are shown for one representative Walker L head; no full-sweep table establishes circuit identity across variants, depths, heads, and widths.

Reviewer-identified: no random-weight or untrained-transformer baseline tests how much normalized-position geometry follows from token embeddings, positional encoding, and uniform averaging before learning.
Reviewer-identified: probes and weight decomposition are not followed by causal ablation, patching, or steering of the proposed world-state axes.

Reviewer-identified: RNNs need only preserve predictive equivalence classes, not necessarily the same human-named position-time state, so must track the same world-state is stronger than the optimality argument.
Reviewer-identified: models are only one or two layers, use horizon 20 and context eight, and train and validate on the exact same process support.
Reviewer-identified: separate models are trained for each constraint, so shared post-attention geometry is not evidence that one model abstracts a reusable world across tasks.
failure_modes: A high reverse-fit R-squared describes only state centroids while individual path activations carry substantial unexplained structure.
Cross-variant CKA is driven by shared positional embeddings and normalized cumulative move counts rather than an abstract task-independent world model.
A random or untrained attention layer with near-uniform weights produces a similar coordinate map.
Random cross-validation rows leak nearby or equivalent state geometry and overstate extrapolative linear readability.
The claimed coordinate stage disappears with longer contexts, new endpoints, shifted obstacle layouts, stochastic transitions, hidden states, or natural sequences.
The MLP's lower coordinate R-squared reflects a harmless invertible nonlinear reparametrization rather than task specialization.
The model uses the proposed directions correlationally but predictions do not change selectively when those axes are patched or ablated.
Different random seeds find equally optimal but geometrically different transformer algorithms, undermining universality.
RNNs encode another minimal sufficient state and are incorrectly judged less world-like because it is not aligned to the chosen coordinate basis.
Bayes-optimal in-distribution prediction fails under length, endpoint, obstacle, or transition-rule shifts.
reusable_insights: Choose synthetic processes whose full-future sufficient state and next-token distribution can be derived separately and exactly.
Construct states with identical next-step outputs but different futures to test whether representations preserve longer-horizon distinctions.
Use both activation-to-target and target-to-activation probes; the latter makes a stronger but aggregation-sensitive claim about explained variance.
Report raw-activation and state-mean results together so path-specific variance is not hidden by geometric averaging.
Compare multiple architectures at matched predictive optimum to expose Rashomon representations that loss alone does not determine.
Analyze how attention and MLP stages separately transform a predictive state, but validate the proposed computation with causal patching or ablation.
Restrict CKA to aligned examples across tasks and disclose how support intersection and aggregation change the result.
Treat near-output target readout as a sanity check when the output head makes it algebraically necessary.
Add distribution shifts even in exactly solvable worlds; in-distribution optimality is not evidence that a coordinate algorithm generalizes.
Use exact process entropy to distinguish optimization failure from representational differences.
open_questions: Do same-configuration training seeds converge to the same attention compass, time code, and world-then-task geometry?
How much of the post-attention result appears in untrained transformers or explicit uniform-averaging baselines?
Do raw individual activations, rather than state means, remain largely spanned by a richer exact sufficient statistic?
Will causal ablation or activation patching of coordinate axes selectively change predicted moves and transfer states across walker variants?
Does the coordinate stage generalize to unseen endpoints, obstacle layouts, horizons, context lengths, and transition rules?
What happens when observation tokens do not deterministically specify state transitions and the predictor must maintain beliefs?
Can one jointly trained model reuse the same post-attention world coordinates across multiple constraint tokens or tasks?
Is post-MLP divergence truly task specialization or an invertible coordinate warp with preserved full-future information?
Which sufficient representation do optimal RNNs use when it is not aligned to normalized human-interpretable coordinates?
Can predictive-statistic theory scale to learned simulators where the sufficient state is estimated rather than known?

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers represent belief state geometry in their residual stream
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest direct antecedent connecting exact predictive sufficient states to transformer residual geometry.
competitive_landscape.difference: Shai et al. already show linearly embedded belief-state geometry and distinctions beyond next-token outputs in HMM and RRXOR processes; this paper extends that program to nonstationary spatial bridges and proposes a specific attention-to-MLP world/task staging.

competitive_landscape.title: Constrained Belief Updates Explain Geometric Structures in Transformer Representations
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest mechanistic antecedent deriving attention algorithms and geometry from predictive statistics.
competitive_landscape.difference: Piotrowski et al. derive constrained Bayesian updates, attention patterns, OV vectors, embeddings, and multilayer refinement for hidden Markov models; this paper substitutes an explicit spatial coordinate and cross-constraint comparison, so the general mechanism-first novelty is substantially overlapped.

competitive_landscape.title: Emergent World Representations: Exploring a Sequence Model Trained on a Synthetic Task
competitive_landscape.difference: Othello-GPT recovers board state and changes outputs through interventions in a more combinatorial game; this paper supplies an exact predictive-statistics derivation and architecture comparison but does not provide comparable causal control.

competitive_landscape.title: Emergent Linear Representations in World Models of Self-Supervised Sequence Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct linear-probing and intervention antecedent on Othello world state.
competitive_landscape.difference: Nanda et al. show a simple player-relative linear board representation and use vector arithmetic to control behavior; this paper analyzes an easier closed-form spatial process and bidirectional span, but leaves its decoded coordinates causally untested.

competitive_landscape.title: What Should Embeddings Embed? Autoregressive Models Represent Latent Generating Distributions
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct theoretical and empirical sufficient-statistics antecedent.
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhang et al. argue from a Bayesian account that autoregressive embeddings should encode predictive sufficient statistics and reconstruct embeddings from those statistics; this paper sharpens one toy setting with affine reverse fits, layer staging, exact grid geometry, and architecture comparisons.

competitive_landscape.title: Cognitive Maps in Language Models: A Mechanistic Analysis of Spatial Planning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest spatial random-walk and causal-map competitor.
competitive_landscape.difference: Baumgartner et al. train GPT-2 on grid foraging and planning, find a map-like coordinate system, and use causal interventions to distinguish map-based from path-dependent algorithms and generalization; this paper provides exact predictive-statistic derivations and constraint universality but no causal or shift test.

competitive_landscape.title: Linearly Structured World Representations in Maze-Solving Transformers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct spatial representation and attention-head antecedent.
competitive_landscape.difference: Ivanitskiy et al. linearly reconstruct maze topology and valid paths and identify adjacency heads in maze-solving transformers; this paper uses random walks rather than solution sequences and relates its coordinate map exactly to predictive distributions.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers learn factored representations
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct contemporary theory of how latent predictive factors occupy transformer subspaces.
competitive_landscape.difference: It derives and tests product-space versus orthogonal factorized representations, including accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs under dependent factors; this paper instead distinguishes a shared full-future state from task-specific next-token geometry across layers and architectures.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural networks leverage nominally quantum and post-quantum representations
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct cross-architecture predictive-state geometry competitor and contrary evidence on architecture dependence.
competitive_landscape.difference: Riechers et al. report future-distribution geometries largely independent of transformer versus RNN architecture for more exotic generators; this paper finds the underlying state readable in both but a clean world/task stage only in attention, making the scope of architecture dependence an open conflict.

competitive_landscape.title: Symmetry in language statistics shapes the geometry of model representations
competitive_landscape.relationship: Competing data-statistics explanation for emergent representation geometry.
competitive_landscape.difference: Karkada et al. derive circles, ripples, and coordinate decodability from translation symmetry in pairwise co-occurrence statistics across embedding and language models; this paper uses full predictive distributions and architectural computation, so pairwise-statistics and sufficient-state explanations need direct ablation against each other.

competitive_landscape.title: Manifold Steering Reveals the Shared Geometry of Neural Network Representation and Behavior
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct causal alternative for testing whether decoded geometry actually shapes outputs.
competitive_landscape.difference: Wurgaft et al. fit activation and behavior manifolds and intervene along curved paths to establish bidirectional geometry-behavior agreement; this paper has stronger analytic ground truth but uses probes and visualization without an equivalent behavioral intervention.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims an analytically grounded demonstration that transformer computation factors into a universal post-attention world-state coordinate system and a later constraint-specific next-token geometry, while equally optimal RNNs do not isolate the same stage.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Its distinctive evidence combines three constrained spatial processes, exact dynamic programming, bidirectional affine fits, a 36-model transformer sweep, common-support cross-variant CKA, attention OV decomposition, and 60 recurrent baselines.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Belief-state geometry beyond next-token outputs, sufficient-statistic reconstruction, and attention-based constrained updates are already established by Shai, Zhang, and Piotrowski; spatial map representations and causal tests also appear in maze and cognitive-map work. The credible novelty is the exact grid-bridge formulation and empirical decomposition of a shared normalized spatial stage versus constraint-specific effective field across separate walker models, plus the matched-optimum RNN comparison. Universal world model, full activation span, and mechanistic implementation should be narrowed until raw-activation, untrained, seed, causal, joint-task, and distribution-shift controls pass.
